answer: Price admission itself: each epoch the slots that let an agent act are auctioned, every bid visible under a lantern-lit order book. Established agents renew seats cheaply, their served-task history earning rebates; a fresh identity pays full clearing price every epoch, no grandfathering. A farm fielding N clones funds N seats at once and bids against itself - each extra clone inflates the price its siblings pay, so fleet cost compounds past N times single entry. Clustered bids from one wallet betray the falcon-strike pattern; those seats void and re-auction, the ember price doing the rest.
